Metadata.title: Fogata — stories around the fire
Metadata.description: A warm home for long-form stories. Read, write and share around the campfire.

headlines: Pull up a seat. Someone is telling a story.
Every great story starts with a spark.
Stay a while. The fire is still warm.
There's always room for one more by the fire.
Some stories take time. Take yours.
Bring a story. Stay for a few more.
The night is young and the fire is lit.
Gather round. This one is worth hearing.

Manifesto.title: Manifesto
Manifesto.description: What we believe at Fogata: reading comes first, your words are yours, and this fire isn't for sale.
Manifesto.lede: There is something very old about sitting around a fire to hear someone tell a story. Before algorithms, before metrics and screens that never end, there was a flame, a circle of half-lit faces and a voice holding up the whole night. Fogata is born from that memory. We aren't trying to invent anything... we want to give words back the place that was taken from them.

sections.title: Reading comes first
sections.body: The internet learned to shout. Every page fills up with windows that jump, ads that follow you around and counters that demand attention as if it were a debt. Not here. When you open a story on Fogata, the text is the only thing that matters: type that breathes, margins that let your eyes rest, quiet around every line. Nothing will pop up over what you're reading. Ever.

sections.title: A .org, not an ad network
sections.body: We don't sell ads, we don't sell your data, and we don't build traps to keep you here longer than you want to stay. We know how the machinery on the other side works: it turns attention into merchandise, outrage into fuel and people into numbers someone else cashes in. We won't play that game. Fogata lives on donations from people who think this fire is worth keeping, and that is enough.

sections.title: Your words are yours
sections.body: What you write here belongs to you. It isn't raw material for training machines or inventory to package and resell. We ask AI crawlers to keep their distance, we reserve your rights on every page, and every story carries your name and its year [as it should]. Your words will never be anyone's hostage.

sections.title: Everyone gets everything
sections.body: There is no premium Fogata, no front row around the fire. Someone publishing their first piece and someone with a thousand stories behind them have exactly the same tools. Badges are a thank-you, not a key: they unlock nothing, they only say that someone is still here, feeding the flame.

sections.title: Quiet by design
sections.body: We don't want your addiction. No endless walls, no alerts buzzing every five minutes to drag you back. We send two kinds of email and nothing else: the link to sign in and, if you want it, one summary a week. Everything else can wait until you come back, whenever you choose to.

sections.title: Two languages, one flame
sections.body: Spanish and English are equal citizens here. Neither is a translation of the other, neither is second-class: the interface, the stories and search speak both in the same voice. Telling a story shouldn't depend on the language you learned to dream in.

sections.title: New voices burn too
sections.body: A first story deserves to be read. We want new writers to find readers in days, not years, circles to gather people around what they care about, and every response to be written with the care of someone sharing the same fire. There are no audiences here... there is company.

Manifesto.closing: This is what we believe. Everything else is kindling: tools, pages, code that can change tomorrow. What doesn't change is the fire, and the promise to tend it together.

termsDoc.title: Terms of use
termsDoc.description: The agreement between you and Fogata.org: your account, your rights over your writing, and how we run the platform.
termsDoc.intro: These terms are the agreement between you and Fogata.org when you read, write or take part on Fogata. By using it, you accept them. We kept them as short and plain as we could.

sections.title: Your account
paragraphs: You need to be at least 13, or the minimum age to use online services where you live. One account per person, and keep access to your email safe: anyone who can open your sign-in links can enter your account.

sections.title: Your writing is yours
paragraphs: You keep all rights to what you publish. To run Fogata, you give us a limited, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free permission to store, show and share your work on Fogata and in the places that point back to it: share previews, notification emails and search results. That permission exists only to operate the service, and it ends when you delete the work or your account (except for copies kept for a limited time in backups). We don't sell your work, and we don't use it or let it be used to train AI.

sections.title: Being here with others
paragraphs: Everything you publish must follow the Content policy. You're responsible for what you post, including having the rights to the text and images you use.

sections.title: Moderation
paragraphs: To keep Fogata safe, we may mark a story as sensitive (NSFW), remove content with a public reason, or suspend accounts that break these terms or the Content policy. If you think we got it wrong, write to hola@fogata.org and we'll take another look.

sections.title: Circles
paragraphs: A circle's owner and editors decide which stories it includes and who can join. They make those decisions within these terms; the stories themselves remain their writers'.

sections.title: Donations and badges
paragraphs: Fogata has no paid tier: everyone gets every feature. Donations through Buy Me a Coffee are voluntary, they don't buy features, and Buy Me a Coffee's terms apply to them. Donors receive the Firekeeper badge for two months per donation. Badges are a thank-you and can be granted, expire or be removed.

sections.title: The service
paragraphs: We work hard to keep Fogata running and to protect your work, but we provide it as it is, without guarantees that it will always be available or free of errors, and we may change or retire features. To the extent the law allows, Fogata.org isn't liable for indirect losses, or for content that others publish.

sections.title: Leaving
paragraphs: You can leave whenever you want by deleting your account in Settings, and download your data first. We may close accounts that seriously or repeatedly break these terms.

sections.title: Law and changes
paragraphs: These terms are governed by the laws of Mexico, without taking away the protections you have as a consumer where you live. If we change them, we'll update the date above and tell you on Fogata about important changes before they apply. Questions: hola@fogata.org.

privacyDoc.title: Privacy policy
privacyDoc.description: What Fogata collects, why, who helps us run it, and your rights over your data.
privacyDoc.intro: Fogata.org is a place to read and write long-form stories. This policy explains what we collect, why we need it, who helps us process it, and what you can do about it. The short version: we don't show ads, we don't sell or rent your data, and we don't use ad trackers.

sections.title: Who is responsible
paragraphs: Fogata.org is responsible for the personal data described here. For anything about your data, write to hola@fogata.org.

sections.title: What we collect
items: Your email address, to sign you in with a one-time link. If you choose Google sign-in, Google shares your email address and name with us.
What you choose to show on your profile: username, name, short bio, photo, links, pronouns, your "Now" line and your influences. All of it is public.

What you publish and do: stories, responses, sparks, embers (passages you highlight), follows, circle memberships and requests to join, reading lists, and the people you mute or block. Published stories and responses are public; drafts, your saved stories and reading lists, your embers, the people you mute or block and your notifications are private. Writers see how many people saved their story and, once two or more readers have kept the same paragraph as an ember, how many did: never who, and never which words.
Your preferences: interface language and how often we may email you. Theme and reading preferences stay in your own browser.
Photos you upload. Your browser resizes them and removes location and camera data (EXIF/GPS) before they reach us.

Anonymous reading counts: when you read a story, we note how far you got and roughly for how long, under a code that changes every day, so your reads can't be linked over time. We don't store your IP address with it. Writers see totals (visits, reads, how far readers got and average reading time), never who read.
Basic technical records that our hosting keeps for a short time to keep the site secure and working, such as IP address and browser type.

sections.title: What we don't do
items: We don't show ads and we don't sell, rent or trade personal data.
We don't use advertising or analytics cookies, and we don't build profiles of you for anyone else.
We don't use your writing to train AI, and we ask AI crawlers not to collect it.

sections.title: Why we use your data
paragraphs: To run your account and show what you publish; to send sign-in links and, if you want it, a weekly activity summary; to keep Fogata safe (preventing abuse and enforcing the Content policy); and to answer you when you write to us. We rely on your consent and on what's necessary to provide the service you asked for.

sections.title: Cookies
paragraphs: We only use cookies that the site needs: one keeps you signed in and another remembers your language. There are no tracking cookies, which is why we don't show a cookie banner.

sections.title: Email
paragraphs: We only send two kinds of email: sign-in links, and a weekly summary of new activity if you leave it on. Every summary has a one-click unsubscribe, and you can turn it off in Settings.

sections.title: Who helps us run Fogata
paragraphs: We use a few service providers, each only for its job: Supabase (database, sign-in and file storage), Vercel (hosting), Resend (sending email) and Google (only if you sign in with Google). On the sign-in page, Cloudflare Turnstile checks that you're a person, without tracking cookies. Photos picked from Unsplash load directly from Unsplash's servers, so Unsplash can see the reader's IP address; it doesn't set cookies on those images. Listen mode uses your browser's own voices: voices on your device read the story right there, and if you pick a voice marked online, your browser sends what's being read to the company behind that voice (such as Google or Microsoft) to speak it. Fogata itself sends nothing. Donations happen on Buy Me a Coffee, under its own privacy policy. These providers may process data in the United States and other countries, under their own security and privacy commitments.

sections.title: How long we keep it
paragraphs: We keep your data while your account exists. If you delete a story, it leaves Fogata at once. If you delete your account, we delete your profile, your stories, your responses and everything else tied to it. Copies can remain in backups for a limited time before they're overwritten.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: You can access, correct, delete and take a copy of your data, and object to how we use it (in Mexico, your ARCO rights; in the EU, your GDPR rights). Most of it you can do yourself: edit your profile in Settings, download your data, or delete your account. For anything else, write to hola@fogata.org and we'll answer within 20 business days.

sections.title: Children
paragraphs: Fogata isn't meant for children under 13, or under the minimum age to use online services where they live.

sections.title: Security
paragraphs: Everything travels encrypted (HTTPS), access to data is restricted by rules in the database itself, and we keep what we collect to a minimum. No system is perfectly secure; if something goes wrong that affects you, we'll tell you.

sections.title: Changes
paragraphs: When this policy changes we'll update the date above, and for important changes we'll let you know on Fogata before they take effect.

contentDoc.title: Content policy
contentDoc.description: What belongs around Fogata's fire, what doesn't, and how to report something.
contentDoc.intro: Fogata is a campfire: people come to tell stories and to listen. Fiction, poetry and essays can go to dark places, and they should be able to. What isn't welcome is harming real people. These rules apply to stories, responses, profiles and circles.

sections.title: Not allowed
items: Any sexual content involving minors. Zero tolerance: we remove it, close the account and report it to the authorities.
Intimate images or sexual content shared without the consent of the people in them.
Threats, incitement to violence or support for violent extremism.
Harassment and bullying, including publishing someone's private information (doxxing).
Attacks on people for their ethnicity, nationality, religion, disability, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation or similar characteristics.
Encouraging suicide, self-harm or eating disorders. Writing about these experiences is welcome; urging others toward them isn't.
Spam, scams, phishing or malware links, and manipulating the platform with fake accounts or coordinated sparks.
Impersonating other people or organizations.
Plagiarism, or publishing work you don't have the rights to.
Anything illegal.

sections.title: Allowed, with a warning
paragraphs: Explicit sexual content between adults and graphic violence can have a place in literature. Moderators may mark those stories as sensitive (NSFW): they open behind a warning that states why, they don't show images in previews, and they stay off the home page, topics, circles and search.

sections.title: Honesty about your work
paragraphs: Publish what you wrote. If a story is largely generated by AI, say so in it.

sections.title: What happens when something breaks the rules
paragraphs: Depending on how serious it is, we may mark it as sensitive, remove it (its address will show the reason), or suspend the account. Illegal content is reported to the authorities. To ask us to review a decision, write to hola@fogata.org.

sections.title: Reporting
paragraphs: Send the link and a short description of the problem to hola@fogata.org. We read every report and keep the reporter's identity private. A report button inside Fogata is on its way.

sections.title: Copyright complaints
paragraphs: If you believe something on Fogata copies your work, write to hola@fogata.org with: the work that's yours, the link on Fogata, your contact details, and a statement that you're the owner or act for them and that the information is accurate. We'll remove what infringes and let the writer know; they can reply if they believe it's a mistake.

Account.title: Your account
Account.lede: Shape your feeds, take a copy of everything you've done on Fogata, or leave for good.
Account.feedBody: The languages you read shape Latest; the topics you follow fill Following.
Account.exportBody: One file with your profile, your stories (drafts included, with their full text), your responses, sparks, saved stories, embers, who you follow and your circles.
Account.deleteBody: This deletes your profile, your stories, your responses, your photos and everything else tied to your account, right away and for good. Circles you own are deleted too. Consider downloading your data first.

errors.unauthorized: Your session ended. Sign in again.
errors.failed: Your account couldn't be deleted. Try again, or write to hola@fogata.org.

Account.blockedBody: People you mute or block can't reach your notifications, home page or story responses. Blocked people also can't follow you or respond to your writing. Nobody is told. Use the … menu on someone's profile to add them here.
Account.blockedEmpty: You haven't muted or blocked anyone.

Stats.title: Stats
Stats.lede: How your stories are being read. Totals only: Fogata never shows you who read, saved or highlighted.
Stats.readRatioHint: Visits that got past half the story
Stats.followersTotal: {count, plural, one {# follower in all} other {# followers in all}}
Stats.chartTitle: Visits and reads, day by day
Stats.chartCaption: Each column is a day's visits (UTC). The darker part is reads: visits that got past half the story.
Stats.chartKeys: Use the left and right arrow keys to move between days.
Stats.emptyPeriod: No visits in the last 30 days yet. Share a story and the first ones will show up here.
Stats.storiesLede: Since each story was published. Reads go back 13 months.
Stats.noStories: Publish a story and its numbers will show up here.
Stats.sparkers: {count, plural, =0 {No sparks yet} one {From # reader} other {From # readers}}
Stats.periodTotals: Last 30 days: {views, plural, one {# visit} other {# visits}}, {reads, plural, one {# read} other {# reads}}.
Stats.depthLede: {count, plural, one {Of # visit, how many reached each point of the page.} other {Of # visits, how many reached each point of the page.}}
Stats.lovedLede: Paragraphs that two or more readers kept as embers. You never see who kept them, or which words they picked.
Stats.lovedReaders: {count, plural, one {# reader kept this} other {# readers kept this}}
Stats.lovedEmpty: When two or more readers keep the same paragraph as an ember, it shows up here.

Join.title: Pull up a seat by the fire
Join.body: Fogata is a home for long-form writing in English and Spanish: free for everyone, with no ads and no paywall. Join to spark this story, follow {name} and keep the stories you love.

Rss.topicDescription: The latest stories about {name} on Fogata.org.

Embed.warning: This story carries a content warning. Open it on Fogata to read it.

Published.title: Your story is live
Published.body: New writers are found through the people who share them. Send it to a few friends who'd enjoy it, or post it where your readers already are.
Published.tip: Everyone you send it to can read the whole story, free, with no sign-up.
